hypothesis.title: The Relation That Survives
hypothesis.question: When a musical variation discards one surface coordinate system, does preserving a named relation make the seed more recognizable than an equally changed variation without that relation?
hypothesis.hypothesis: If a variation preserves a declared relation such as voice-leading adjacency, spatial distance pattern, prosodic contour, or band-energy independence while changing surface coordinates, then listeners will rate the seed as more recognizable than in a control variation with comparable surface change but no preserved relation.
hypothesis.rationaleMd: S1 shows that harmonic resources can be represented as combinatorial configurations where incidence and adjacency, rather than isolated chord labels, organize musical possibility. S5 gives an acoustic parallel: exploiting Euclidean Distance Matrix and Gram-matrix relations reduces localization from direct three-coordinate optimization to lower-dimensional relational geometry. S3 separates voice into static timbre and dynamic prosody, suggesting that identity and contour can be varied independently. S4 reports that speech-enhancement encoders preserve noise-invariant representations while decoders adapt to degradation, supporting an invariant-skeleton/adaptive-surface distinction. S6 shows that decomposed and fused multi-band representations outperform baseband-only approaches in bioacoustics, while S2 warns that real systems follow reachable paths rather than all mathematically valid configurations. Together these sources support a testable compositional claim: continuity can be carried by preserved relations under coordinate loss, but only when the transformation remains perceptually reachable.

recipe.title: Coordinate-Loss Variations
recipe.bodyMd: Compose a 60-second study from a four-bar seed. Make four variations that each discard one coordinate system while preserving one relation: preserve a Tonnetz-like voice-leading adjacency path while changing voicing/register/instrumentation [S1]; preserve a near/far or left/right distance relation between two sources while changing absolute spatial placement [S5]; preserve a melodic/prosodic contour while swapping source identity, or preserve source identity while changing contour [S3]; and preserve a low/mid/high/air band relation while allowing each band to change independently before fusion [S6]. Keep tempo, form length, seed rhythm, and integrated loudness constant. Compare each relation-preserving version with a control that changes a similar amount of surface detail without preserving the target relation. If relation-preserving versions are not more recognizable than controls, the hypothesis is not supported for this material.

parameters.value: four broad bands: low, mid, high, air

dawChecklist: Create a 60-second session at 120 BPM and write one four-bar seed.
Duplicate the seed into four variation lanes plus four control lanes.
Variation 1: preserve the voice-leading adjacency path while changing voicing, register, and instrumentation.
Variation 2: preserve the two-source spatial distance pattern while changing absolute pan, delay, or reverb placement.
Variation 3: preserve contour while swapping source identity, or preserve identity while changing contour.
Variation 4: split the texture into low, mid, high, and air bands, vary each independently, then fuse them into one gesture.
For each control lane, change a comparable amount of surface detail without preserving the target relation.
Level-match all lanes and keep tempo, seed rhythm, form length, and integrated loudness constant.
Render blind comparison clips and score recognizability, transformedness, and relation clarity.

protocol.listeningContext: Level-matched headphones or nearfields; compare relation-preserving variations against matched controls without looking at arrangement lanes.
protocol.listeningMethod: For each pair, score whether the seed remained recognizable, whether the material felt transformed rather than copied, and which relation carried continuity.

notes: Falsification criterion: if relation-preserving variations are not rated more recognizable than matched controls, or if they are recognizable only because too many surface coordinates stayed fixed, the relation-survival framing is not useful for this material.
